faithful_summary: Full 2023 annual review. Technical claims translated faithfully: x64 builds are being tested by community members; WoW64 is absent in this article's snapshot, with a large list of x64 apps shown (NewMoon, SumatraPDF, PeaZip, PuTTY, Notepad++, eMule, Firefox, Gimp 2.8, ClassicCube 1.3.x). ARM section: FreeLoader was booted on a Lumia 950XL; many system components and drivers are not ported to ARM, but user applications compile for ARM and run in Windows on that architecture. A TCP/IP driver change by Doug Lyons accepts 0xFFFF as a valid port number and is said to fix a BSoD after hours or days of network use; a member reported over 30 days of network uptime. An NTFS boot sector implemented in late August 2023 loads FreeLdr from an NTFS partition, but the article states there is no stable NTFS driver and testing requires extra manual steps. On 19 November 2023 registry repair/verification work was merged; forced shutdown after a hang, BSoD or VM reboot could previously corrupt the registry and cause a BSoD or a stuck Ctrl-Alt-Del logon. Late-June win32k DirectX patches are said to enable hardware acceleration by replacing XP/2003 ddraw.dll, d3d8.dll, d3d9.dll and dxg.sys; the article says testing so far was in a VM. Chromium 49 works with --no-sandbox but the mouse sticks; the author calls these unfinished work. Community comments mention PR #4571 registry transaction improvements and nightlies 0.4.15+ largely avoiding the reboot failure.

faithful_summary: Full German article on LiberNT, a ReactOS fork. Technical claims translated faithfully: the previous ReactOS ARM3 memory manager was removed and replaced by 'NT Virtual Memory Subsystem' (NVS) with its own kernel memory management; the cache manager was rewritten. Work covers WDDM with DWM, a new NTFS driver, xHCI and PCI Express support; the article explicitly says code presence does not necessarily mean components work fully. Targets are AMD64, ARM64 and RISC-V; images exist for those architectures and Raspberry Pi support is planned. WoW64 is intended for 32-bit Windows apps, with FEX emulation planned for x86 code on ARM64; some features are experimental or require explicit build flags. Generative AI is used for writing, reviewing, debugging and evaluating documentation, with human review claimed before merge.

faithful_summary: Full Spanish article reporting the project's response to abandonment rumours. Technical claims translated faithfully: the three-month release cadence was changed because quantity outranked quality; a stable release now requires no more than 20 regressions and no severe stability impact from new features. The 64-bit x86 port is described as early but steadily more stable, previously hanging or blue-screening at startup; because WoW64 is absent, 32-bit software cannot yet run. The SepAccessCheck hack, which granted access regardless of security descriptor restrictions, was removed. Registry corruption has no automatic recovery and can leave the system stuck at logon; a developer was working on automatic recovery and CmCheckRegistry, but that work enlarged the loader and prevented the x86_64 build from booting. Btrfs is mentioned as a filesystem choice to reduce corruption; Japanese IME input in CMD and the rich-text editor was still unavailable and there were stability glitches.
next_action: Check whether CmCheckRegistry enlargement and x64 boot interaction was later resolved.
